notes.meaning: Peace at home is worth much more than plenty of food with arguing. A dry crust of bread eaten in a quiet, loving house brings far more joy than rich banquet meats in a home full of fighting. Love and contentment make even the simplest meal sweet.

A servant who acts with wisdom can rise higher than a son who brings shame on the family. Over time, such a faithful servant may even be put in charge of the household and receive a share of the family inheritance. Good character and wise choices matter more than family privilege alone.

Silversmiths use intense heat in melting pots and furnaces to burn away impurities from silver and gold. In a similar way, the Lord tests and refines human hearts through life's trials. Only God can see deep inside us to reveal what needs to be made pure.

People with wicked hearts love to listen to harmful speech and slander. A liar eagerly welcomes gossip and deceit because it matches their own corrupt desires. What someone enjoys listening to reveals what kind of person they really are.

Making fun of poor people is an insult to God, who created them and cares for them. In the same way, taking pleasure when disaster strikes someone else is a serious sin. God sees cruel hearts and will not let such malice go unpunished.

Grandchildren bring honor and delight to grandparents, resting on them like a crown. At the same time, children take pride in having good and godly parents. A loving family where each generation honors the other is a rich blessing from God.

Fine and noble words sound completely out of place coming from a corrupt fool whose life contradicts them. It is far worse when a ruler or leader tells lies to the people. Those in authority should show noble character by always speaking the truth.

To the person offering or accepting it, a bribe looks like a magical jewel that opens every door. The proverb observes how money easily sways selfish people and makes them bend the rules. It describes how the corrupt world operates without approving of dishonest gain.

A person who chooses to forgive and overlook an offense helps love to flourish. On the other hand, someone who keeps repeating old grievances and gossiping about them ruins close friendships. True peace is preserved when we choose not to bring up past wrongs.

A single gentle word of correction cuts deep into the heart of a wise and understanding person. A stubborn fool, however, will not learn a lesson even after a hundred blows. A humble heart is ready to listen, but pride refuses to change.

A rebellious person constantly looks for ways to stir up trouble and resist authority. Because of this, a harsh officer or judgment will be sent to stop them without mercy. Resisting God and lawful order brings swift and painful consequences.

A mother bear whose cubs have been taken is wild with rage and highly dangerous. Yet it is far safer to cross paths with an angry bear than with a fool lost in his reckless folly. Uncontrolled human anger turns a person into someone worse than a wild animal.

Paying back evil to someone who showed you kindness is a terrible violation of God's ways. Anyone who treats a benefactor with cruelty invites lasting misery into their own household. Ingratitude brings a heavy curse that can affect an entire family.

Starting an argument is like breaking a small hole in a water dam. The leak quickly widens until a destructive flood rushes through and sweeps everything away. It is far better to drop a disagreement immediately before tempers boil over.

Letting a guilty person walk free and punishing an innocent person are both repulsive to the Lord. Both actions corrupt justice and blur the sacred line between right and wrong. God demands honest judgment from every court and leader.

Having money in hand to pay for an education is completely useless to a fool who has no real desire to learn. Wisdom cannot simply be bought with cash if someone lacks humility and the fear of the Lord. Great opportunities are wasted without a willing heart.

A genuine friend stays faithful and loving through every season of life. When trouble comes, that friend stands by you like a brother born specifically to help carry the burden. True companionship shines brightest during times of deep hardship.

It is foolish to make a rash promise to pay off someone else's debt. Shaking hands to guarantee a loan can easily bring financial ruin on your own family. True charity should never be confused with reckless financial pledges.

Anyone who loves picking fights is really showing a love for sin. In the same way, building a flashy, towering gate to show off wealth is an act of pride that invites ruin. Both quarrelsomeness and boasting spring from arrogance and lead straight to disaster.

A person with a crooked and deceitful mind will never find true happiness. Someone who uses their tongue to spread lies and stir up trouble will soon fall into ruin. Dishonesty always ends up harming the person who practices it.

Raising a child who grows up to be foolish and wicked brings constant grief to a father. Instead of the joy parents long for, a foolish life causes ongoing heartbreak at home. Parents must often bear this heavy trial with patience and prayer.

A joyful heart works like good medicine that brings strength and healing to the body. On the other hand, sadness, anxiety, and a crushed spirit drain a person's energy and dry up the bones. Our inner spiritual state has a direct impact on our physical well-being.

A corrupt person takes a secret bribe slipped from beneath a robe to twist the outcome of a case. Taking money in secret ruins justice and deprives innocent people of fair treatment. God hates all bribery because it turns right into wrong.

An understanding person keeps wisdom right in front of them as their steady goal. A fool, however, lets their eyes and thoughts wander aimlessly to the ends of the earth. Chasing distant fantasies keeps a person from noticing the practical truth right nearby.

A foolish child brings heavy sorrow to his father and bitter heartache to the mother who gave him birth. Both parents share the painful weight of seeing their child reject wise guidance. The choices of a child deeply affect the entire home.

It is completely wrong for judges to fine an innocent person or to beat an honorable leader for acting with integrity. God gives authority to rulers to protect good people, not to mistreat them. Using the law to attack upright people brings serious guilt on any court.

A person with real knowledge knows how to choose words carefully and stay quiet when needed. Someone with true understanding keeps a cool temper and remains calm under pressure. Keeping control over speech and temper is a sure sign of wise character.

Even a foolish person can be considered wise if they simply know how to keep their mouth shut. By staying quiet, they hide their lack of good sense and appear thoughtful to others. Learning when not to speak is one of the most useful lessons in wisdom.
